item.description: K–Ar dating reveals >110 Myr of episodic Altyn Tagh Fault activity, beginning at ~115 Ma along a Cretaceous lithospheric weakness. Reactivation at ~56 Ma records rapid India–Asia collisional stress transmission >1500 km into the continental interior. The rate and efficiency of stress transmission across continental interiors during collision remain poorly constrained. The >1600-km-long Altyn Tagh Fault, bounding the northern Tibetan Plateau, offers a key test of stress propagation models. Here, we integrate multiscale structural analysis with K–Ar dating of synkinematic illite to date its faulting history. The data document episodic faulting spanning >110 million years, including an ~115 Ma event marking a lithospheric weakness zone predating Cenozoic collision, and an Early Eocene faulting age (~56 Ma), which is nearly synchronous with India–Asia collision onset, implying rapid far-field stress transmission across distances exceeding 1500 km within 10 million years of collision initiation. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict. item.dc:creator: Ke Zhu

item.description: Abstract Micrometeorite bombardment is a fundamental surface process on the Moon and other airless bodies, driving elemental evaporation, isotopic fractionation, and material mixing in surface regoliths. Here, we report high-precision stable Ni isotope data for lunar soils returned by the Apollo (11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17) and Chang’e (5 and 6) missions, covering geographically and geologically diverse lunar terrains. The analyzed soils show δ 60/58 Ni values of 0.345‰ to 1.280‰ (relative to NIST SRM 986), generally heavier than lunar basalts and the inferred bulk silicate Moon, indicating widespread heavy Ni isotope enrichment during surface processing. Together with published Chang’e-5 drill-core data, these results demonstrate that micrometeorite-driven Ni isotope fractionation is widespread across the lunar surface. Local variability, however, reflects additional controls. The relatively low δ 60/58 Ni values of the immature Apollo 12 soils are consistent with limited cumulative micrometeorite processing, whereas the mature Apollo 16 soils have high Ni concentrations and Ni/Co ratios, indicating additional compositional overprinting by Ni-rich material. Stable Ni isotopes, particularly when combined with regolith maturity and Ni/Co ratios, therefore provide a sensitive tracer of micrometeorite-driven lunar surface processing and its local overprinting. item.description: While mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB) and ocean island basalts (OIB) are well characterized in terms of helium, neon, argon, and xenon isotopes, the continental lithosphere, especially cratonic domains and subduction settings, remain poorly constrained. Here, we report noble gas (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, and Xe) isotope ratios in peridotite, pyroxenite, and eclogite xenoliths from the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton, Brazil. Helium isotopes reveal a strong radiogenic component, while neon shows MORB-like and nucleogenic signatures. This divergence indicates the recycling of subduction-derived materials within the stratified cratonic mantle (2.0–5.5 GPa). Xenon reveals a cratonic lithosphere where air and fissiogenic (crustal) components variably mix with a MORB source. The recycling of ancient hydrated oceanic crust and overlying sediments, characterized by high (U+Th)/(^3He, ^22Ne, ^132Xe) ratios, is associated with a complex and long-lived subduction system established along the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton since the Archean. This study reveals that noble gas isotopes in mantle rocks beneath the São Francisco Craton, Brazil, record the recycling of volatiles from Archean subduction into the continental mantle. item.title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
item.dc:creator: Jung-Hun Song

item.description: Abstract Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet. item.title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Naveed Zafar

item.description: In Lake Iseo, Italy, human-driven erosion amplified sediment accumulation and preconditioned the delta for catastrophic earthquake-induced collapses and tsunamis, revealing a global mechanism linking human land use to increasing tsunami hazards in lakes. Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Here we show from geological records and numerical simulations that earthquakes in 1117 CE (Mw 6.5) and 1222 CE (Mw 6.0) triggered major subaqueous delta collapses, generating massive tsunamis with maximum run-ups of ~50 m and ~13 m, respectively. Historical accounts from the Vatican Library and archeological evidence support these reconstructions. Since the last collapse, eight centuries of human-induced erosion have rebuilt the delta, leaving shoreline populations highly vulnerable to future earthquake-triggered failures. A global lake synthesis showed that human-driven erosion has reached its highest levels since the Industrial Era, progressively overloading deltas worldwide; thus, similar catastrophic failures may become more likely in the future. These findings reveal a persistent, human-amplified mechanism of lacustrine tsunami generation and intensity with major implications for hazard assessment. item.title: Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO2 mineralization
item.dc:creator: Zihua Shao
Yunfeng Liang
Gyuhwan Jo
Keisuke Nakamura
Takeshi Tsuji
item.description: Abstract Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO 2 mineralization. However, the origin of the striking reactivity difference between Ca- and Mg-bearing olivine remains poorly understood. Here we show that this difference arises not merely from the type of cation, but more fundamentally from how these cations modulate the oxygen reactivity. Nonbridging oxygens serve as the oxygen source for CO 2 surface reactions, which in Ca-olivine reduce the Ca 2+ dissolution barrier by 60% and accelerate ion release by six orders of magnitude. The calculated apparent dissolution rate constants reproduce the experimentally observed complete conversion of Ca-olivine within hours under 1 atm CO 2 . This multiscale framework reveals how surface reactions govern silicate carbonation and provides a predictive basis for modeling and engineering large-scale CO 2 mineralization in both synthetic materials and basaltic reservoirs. item.description: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. item.description: Abstract Volcanic deposits preserved within Antarctic fumarolic ice caves provide rare access to sub-ice eruptive records hidden beneath the ice cap. Here we present the first integrated textural, petrological, and geochemical characterisation of 21 tephra samples from three summit ice caves at Mount Melbourne (Northern Victoria Land, Antarctica). Major and trace-element glass compositions, combined with published datasets, were analysed using multivariate statistical workflows. Dimensionality reduction and clustering identified a distinct compositional group with no known equivalent in the existing Mount Melbourne record, suggesting that at least one previously unrecognised Holocene eruption occurred within the investigated Fumarolic Ice Caves. Correspondence between Fumarolic Ice Cave deposits and volcanic signatures in marine sediment, englacial sequences, and other proximal-distal records refined Mount Melbourne’s eruptive history and strengthened tephra correlations across archives. More broadly, sub-ice tephra archives can reveal hidden eruptive histories relevant to volcanic hazard assessment in polar regions. item.dc:creator: Winnie X. Fan

item.description: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle. item.description: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain. item.description: Abstract Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. We find that calcium released by mineral weathering is associated with soil organic carbon storage and that this effect is stronger in Mollisols than in non-Mollisols. Our model also shows that agriculture has increased calcium inputs to cultivated USA Mollisols 4-5 fold, indicating that humans have fundamentally changed the geochemical conditions that sustain organic carbon in these soils. By implication, moderating the quantity of and timing of calcium release may help to preserve and restore carbon in the world’s most intensively farmed landscapes. item.dc:creator: Martin Yan Hei Li
Mei-Fu Zhou
item.description: Abstract Zircon is conventionally considered as refractory in supergene environments, enabling the preservation of geochemical records for tracing various Earth’s processes and the use of the zircon structure as a nuclear waste form. Non-formula elements, like U, Th and heavy rare earth elements, are uptake and structurally incorporated in this process. Thereby, metamictisation of the zircon would accelerate and eventually promote the dissolution of zircon. In supergene environments, zircon would steadily weather, calling for further evaluation on the geological and environmental applications of zircon. item.description: Chemical heterogeneities in Earth’s deep mantle may record either preserved primordial reservoirs or later core-mantle exchange, but distinguishing between these origins remains challenging. item.description: The land-to-ocean export of carbon via rivers is a key component in the global carbon cycle. Integrating these large datasets with mechanistic studies of biogeochemical modulators and machine learning approaches would inform understanding of carbon dynamics within major watersheds and improve predictions of this globally important carbon flux. item.description: Abstract The Jiaodong gold province, with proven resources of more than 5,700 tonnes, is the largest gold-producing region in China. The Jiaodong lamprophyres, monzodiorites, and mafic microgranular enclaves were derived from a common metasomatized mantle lithosphere source but followed distinct evolutionary pathways. Lamprophyres represent relatively primitive mantle-derived magmas that mainly experienced fractional crystallization, whereas the monzodiorites and MMEs represent more evolved magmas that underwent variable degrees of crustal contamination and magma mixing. Chalcophile element geochemistry indicates that sulfide segregation during lamprophyre magma evolution was limited. Consequently, the Au concentrations of the lamprophyres closely reflect the primary Au contents of their parent magmas (0.24–2.34 ng/g). In contrast, the evolved monzodiorites and MMEs experienced significant sulfide segregation and contain lower Au concentrations (0.05–0.60 ng/g). Overall, the Jiaodong mantle-derived magmas did not possess an unusually large magmatic Au budget compared to global magmas genetically associated with magmatic-hydrothermal Au systems (1.30–5.50 ng/g). item.description: Abstract We integrate major and trace element data with high-precision Pb isotope analyses of ores from the Middle Miocene felsic volcanic-hosted massive sulfide deposits of northeast Japan, including the Matsumine-Shakanai, Furutobe, and Nurukawa deposits, to elucidate the distribution and source of precious metals. item.description: The transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision is a key mechanism for understanding orogenic architecture and continental crustal growth. Within this framework, the geodynamic evolution of the Neo-Tethyan slab remains a subject of intensive debate concerning the formation of the Tibetan Plateau. Zircons from the diorite-porphyry and granite dykes have positive εHf(t) values of +9.0 to +11.2 and +11.9 to +13.8, respectively. The coexistence of these two dyke suites provides evidence for slab-window development beneath the central segment of the southern Lhasa subterrane at approximately 47 Ma. item.dc:creator: Xinyi Zhong

item.description: Subduction initiation is a fundamental geodynamic process in plate tectonics, yet its mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the scarcity of geological records. Proposed geological records of subduction initiation, including metamorphic soles, fore-arc basalts and fore-arc sediments, are typically associated with spontaneous subduction initiation in hot environments involving mantle upwelling. In contrast, evidence for the more common cold subduction initiation at continental margins is sparse or even absent. Arc volcanic rocks are widely regarded as direct evidence of subduction zones, particularly for identifying ancient subduction zones in orogens. However, the temporal relationship between subduction initiation and the onset of arc volcanism remains poorly constrained. Although arc volcanism is generally considered to develop within ∼10 million years (Myr) of initiation, our analysis of subduction events over the past 15 Myr reveals a highly variable time lag ranging from 2 to 10 Myr. In this study, we investigate the factors controlling this time lag in forced subduction initiation at continental margins, using a newly developed two-phase flow numerical model that incorporates melt transport and melt extraction processes. Our results show that rapid partial melting at shallow depths, primarily driven by high convergence rates, leads to a shorter time lag between subduction initiation and arc volcanism, which is consistent with observations from recent subduction events. These findings suggest that arc volcanic rocks, when considered together with slab age and convergence rate, provide a useful constraint on the timing of subduction initiation in ancient subduction systems. item.description: Abstract Stable and radiogenic isotopes trace fluid and metal sources in volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS) deposits and discriminate between superimposed mineral systems in ancient terrains. In contrast, sulfide minerals in the stratigraphic hanging wall record heavier δ 34 S values (up to 5.3 ‰ in sphalerite) reflecting syn-diagenetic incorporation of Paleoproterozoic seawater sulfur under anoxic conditions. item.description: Granite-related U deposits are generally spatially related to pre-existing granites with the crystallization ages of granites significantly earlier than the mineralization ages. To address this issue, this study took the Lujing U deposit formed in Cretaceous–Paleogene as the research object. We carried out in situ geochronological and geochemical studies on apatite, monazite, and xenotime from the silicified fault zone, which was previously considered to be formed synchronously with mineralization, and on the zircon from the pre - existing alkali-altered granite. We discovered that the LA-ICP-MS U-Pb geochronology of the accessory minerals in the silicified fault zone and hydrothermal zircon in the granite reveals two Triassic hydrothermal activities at ∼235 Ma and ∼215 Ma, which are synchronous with regional Triassic magmatism. We therefore suggest the Triassic magmatism induced strong alkali metasomatism and the formation of silicified fault zones, which represents pre-ore, rather than syn-ore, hydrothermal activities. Mineral-element geochemistry shows that the ∼215 Ma granite has higher U concentrations than the ∼235 Ma granite. This implies that, in addition to fractional crystallization, repeated melting in the source is another important process that enhances magma fertility, as corroborated by thermodynamic modeling. The apatite from the silicified fault zone shows high Mn content (5,400–27,235 ppm), low δEu values (0.07–0.16), and high XF/XCl ratios (460–6,590). Meanwhile, the monazite from the silicified fault zone exhibits low As content (<1,000 ppm) and high Th content (99,750–207,365 ppm). The geochemical signatures indicate that the Triassic magmatic fluids were characterized by high F and low oxygen fugacity. These attributes were explained to cause the precipitation of U in the fluid via isomorphism in U-rich accessory minerals (monazite, xenotime, apatite, and uranothorite), along with minor uraninite, in granite and silicified fault zone. Therefore, we concluded that the Triassic pre-ore magmatic-hydrothermal event served as a U pre-enrichment stage for the Cretaceous–Paleogene U mineralization. This mineralization was achieved via the circulation of oxidizing fluids rich in Cl− and CO2 in Cretaceous–Paleogene, which are favorable for U dissolution. item.description: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Numerous studies have investigated its stable metal isotope character to understand its formation and secular evolution. Molybdenum (Mo) isotopes are useful tracers of petrogenetic processes in Phanerozoic igneous rocks, but Archean granitoids, which make up much of Earth’s early continental crust, remain poorly characterized. Here, we report high-precision whole-rock Mo isotope data for 28 Archean granitoids from Australia’s Pilbara and Yilgarn cratons, with crystallization ages from 3.52 to 2.63 Ga. The samples cover a spectrum of magmatic series, including tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG), TTG hybrid, sanukitoid, potassic, and potassic hybrid magmas. After assessing the effects of alteration, crustal contamination, and fluid exsolution, we interpret the observed δ 98/95Mo range of − 0.93 to 0.25‰ as primarily reflecting magmatic source characteristics. TTG and TTG hybrid granitoids, together with samples derived from unenriched meta-mafic or mantle-like sources, have mean and median δ 98/95Mo values close to, or slightly higher than, chondrite and depleted MORB mantle (DMM). In contrast, potassic, potassic hybrid, and sanukitoid series granitoids, as well as samples derived from enriched meta-mafic or felsic crustal sources, extend to lower, sub-mantle δ 98/95Mo values. Elemental proxy relationships, major- and trace-element modeling, and phase-equilibrium constraints indicate that source composition and residual mineralogy during partial melting primarily control Mo isotope variability in these rocks. In crustally-derived granitoids, lower δ 98/95Mo values are associated with more mature source compositions and with changes in the abundance and composition of residual feldspar. Amphibole, garnet, and biotite may also have subordinate effects. These relationships suggest that Mo isotopes track the progressive reworking of Archean crust. Juvenile crust-derived TTG magmatism is characterized by near- to suprachondritic δ 98/95Mo, whereas later sanukitoid and potassic granitoid magmatism, linked respectively to mantle metasomatism and reworking of TTG-dominated gray gneiss, shifts toward lower δ 98/95Mo values. The observed trends imply that intracrustal reworking alone can push continental averages to sub-mantle values, with ramifications for mass-balance models. Although TTGs are generally suprachondritic, their δ 98/95Mo values are not high enough to easily support models requiring large volumes of Hadean to Paleoarchean continental extraction from a chondritic mantle to offset the subchondritic Mo isotope composition inferred for the depleted mantle from Archean komatiites. The strong Mo isotope contrast between continental crust and upper mantle may therefore have developed after 2.6 Ga, once crustal recycling became more extensive. item.description: Since the Permian Tarim Large Igneous Province (270–290 Ma) was first recognized, debate has centered on whether to include coeval igneous rocks from the southern Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB). item.description: Marine carbonate archives provide key insights into Earth’s evolving redox state and planetary habitability, preserving carbon-isotope perturbations such as the Lomagundi–Jatuli Event (LJE; ca. 2.22–2.06 Ga), a major global event within the broader interval of the Great Oxidation Event (GOE; ca. 2.45–2.06 Ga). All tourmaline types display ferromagnesian compositions, primarily consisting of dravite, except for TurIV, which has a Cr-rich schorl composition. TurIV represents an evolution toward a more oxidized, low-salinity, and H2O-rich environment, which might be linked to deep-circulating fluids during late-stage tectonic events. item.description: We present new trace element data for chromitites from a six-km mantle section of the Oman ophiolite for samples with a range of compositions between high-alumina and high-chrome chromitites. item.title: Hot Archean orogens suppressed voluminous S-type granite formation
item.dc:creator: Ming Tang
Zi Ye
Xu Chu
item.description: S-type granites are far less abundant during much of the Archean than in the Phanerozoic, and this paucity remains puzzling. We propose that the suppression of S-type granite formation at scale may have been an inherent consequence of the hotter Archean crust. A key insight from fossil P-T-t paths in representative orogens is that the onset of melting can trigger exhumation and thereby limit the maximum burial depth of sediments.​ In a hot crust, this maximum burial depth is relatively shallow, because hot geotherms initiate melting at shallow depths due to the pressure dependence of dehydration melting. By contrast, colder geotherms in Phanerozoic orogens effectively suppress melting until higher pressures and temperatures. As a result, Archean sedimentary packages were exhumed too early to undergo extensive decompression and dehydration melting attainable in modern cycles. Phase equilibria modeling shows that the exhuming metasediments in the Archean may only generate melt fractions 1/3 to 1/2 of those in the Phanerozoic. Such low melt productivity in the Archean may have inhibited the formation of large S-type plutons and batholiths. More broadly, these processes may have impeded deep recycling of sediments and, by limiting upward distillation of heat-producing elements, slowed the cooling of the Archean continental crust. item.description: Advances in high‐resolution in situ techniques, such as SIMS and LA‐ICP‐MS, now enable precise multiple sulfur isotope measurements at spatial resolutions of tens of micrometres, providing new insights into redox evolution, metal behaviour and fluid pathways in ore‐forming systems. All uncertainties are reported as 2 s of replicate bulk analyses (Niko n = 3; Sacra n = 3). SIMS analyses showed lower measurement repeatability for Niko (δ 34 S = 0.39‰, and Δ 33 S = 0.151‰; 2 s , n = 35) as compared with Sacra (0.98‰ and Δ 33 S = 0.330‰, 2 s , n = 44). item.title: Spatiotemporal framework of Deposit-Structure-Magma and fluid migration path in the Zhaxikang Pb-Zn-Sb polymetallic Deposit: Construction of a metallogenic model
item.dc:creator: Guo Jing

item.description: Since the India-Eurasia continental collision, the Tethyan Himalaya has undergone distinctive tectono-magmatic events, including the emplacement of leucogranites and the development of the South Tibetan Detachment System (STDS). These processes have generated a series of Pb-Zn-Sb-Au deposits that are closely tied to tectono-magmatic activity. However, the spatiotemporal relationships between structures, magmatism, and mineralization, as well as the pathways for fluid migration, remain poorly constrained. This gap in understanding has impeded both the development of a robust metallogenic theory and the deployment of effective exploration strategies. This study focuses on the Zhaxikang Pb-Zn-Sb polymetallic deposit, the largest and most extensively studied deposit in the belt. We integrate multi-scale geophysical surveys, carbonaceous Raman spectroscopy thermometry, and 40Ar-39Ar geochronology to achieve the following objectives: (1) construct a comprehensive spatiotemporal framework linking the deposit to regional structures and magmatism; (2) delineate the ore-forming fluid migration pathways; and (3) propose a new metallogenic model and exploration approach. Our results demonstrate that:(1) A low-resistivity, low-density, partially molten layer exists at a depth of 10–15 km beneath Zhaxikang. The east–west trending regional fault F1-1 directly connects this deep molten layer to the shallow orebody, forming a vertical fluid transport system. (2) A multi-scale fault network (F1-2 throw ≈ 1.67 km, F2-2 throw ≈ 1.44 km, F3-1 throw ≈ 328 m, V ore vein throw ≈ 172–326 m) controls long-distance, multi-stage fluid migration. (3) The 40Ar-39Ar age of muscovite from the F1-1 fault (18.9 Ma) is highly consistent with the main Sb mineralization stage in the ore cluster (17.9–12.2 Ma), confirming this fault’s key role in ore formation. Based on these results, we propose a “Zhaxikang-type” tectono-magmatic coupling metallogenic model. In this model, persistent partial melting, coupled with multi-stage fault activity, generates a “seismic pump” suction effect. This mechanism drives ore-forming fluids to migrate over long distances through an interconnected, multi-level fault network, resulting in the multi-stage mineralization observed at Zhaxikang from 43.1 Ma to the present. Following this theoretical framework, we traced the fluid migration path and detected a concealed ore vein (VIe) anomaly 750 m east of the Ve ore vein, successfully completing a loop from theoretical construction to exploration verification. This study not only establishes a new metallogenic paradigm for the Tethyan Himalayan Pb-Zn-Sb-Au belt in a collisional orogenic setting but also provides a transferable methodological framework for exploring deposits formed by long-distance fluid migration.
